definitions.explanation: An event or revelation that damages someone's reputation, especially in public life. A formal, literary equivalent of the loanword スキャンダル.

examples.japanese: ⟦{政治家|せいじか}→政治家：03084_seijika⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{醜聞|しゅうぶん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{報|ほう}じられた→報じる：17193_houjiru⟧。
{醜聞|しゅうぶん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{相次|あいつ}ぎ、{党|とう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{支持率|しじりつ}→支持率：17086_shijiritsu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{急落|きゅうらく}→急落：09399_kyuuraku⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Scandals came one after another, and the party's approval rating plummeted.

examples.japanese: ⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧⟦{企業|きぎょう}→企業：00225_kigyou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{醜聞|しゅうぶん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧まみれて、ついに⟦{倒産|とうさん}→倒産：03452_tousan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{追|お}い{込|こ}まれた→追い込む：06371_oikomu⟧。
examples.english: That company was mired in scandals and was eventually driven into bankruptcy.

notes:
USAGE:
{醜聞|しゅうぶん} is a formal, written-style word. In everyday conversation, スキャンダル is more commonly used. {醜聞|しゅうぶん} appears in news articles, literary works, and formal speech.

ETYMOLOGY:
Composed of {醜|しゅう} (ugly) and {聞|ぶん} (news, report) — literally "ugly news."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {醜聞|しゅうぶん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{発覚|はっかく}する→発覚する：15423_hakkakusuru⟧ (a scandal comes to light)
- {醜聞|しゅうぶん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧まみれる (to be mired in scandal)
- {醜聞|しゅうぶん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{暴|あば}く→暴く：04607_abaku⟧ (to expose a scandal)
